text:
Kiel’s median asking rent sits at 11.27 €/m² in June 2026, up 4.8 % year‑on‑year and 28.8 % over the past five years, placing the city 21st of the 37 most expensive German markets. The 60 m² benchmark rent is 676 € per month, while the asking premium over existing rents is 48 %, reflecting a strong upward momentum.

The market remains balanced with a vacancy rate of 1.6 % and an average of 23 days on market; 30 % of listings are let within a week. Rent‑burden for two residents is 16.2 %, indicating limited affordability despite modest population growth of 0.2 % over five years.

The model‑based forecast projects the median asking rent at 11.89 €/m² in 12 months, ranging between 11.61 €/m² and 12.14 €/m², implying a further 5.5 % rise.
